Priya Patel: Share security whitepaper, KMS & VPC diagram (due: 2026-05-20)

summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Mariner Payments through Optimize recommendations focused on batch sizing and prefix / KV cache tradeoffs. Customer is evaluation-ready for a pilot; primary concerns are 99th percentile latency under peak traffic and compliance (KMS, VPC). Agreed next steps include pricing and a benchmark pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood — i'm the AE on the account. we got priya here from the SE team as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sam Torres: good, thanks. we, uh, excited to see the Optimize walkthrough. quick heads up — we only got 56 minutes so maybe we go through the recommendations and then Q&A.
[00:14] Priya Patel: sounds good. agenda: we'll cover current infra, batching basics, prefix K V cache (i'll say KV cache), expected hit rates, cost model impacts, and then pilot steps.
[00:25] Mark Delaney: perfect. our main asks are predictable 99th pct latency <200ms for user-facing flows and keeping cost to a reasonable multiple of current infra.
[00:33] Alex Chen: got it, that's helpful. Sam or lena, can you remind us of your current stack? where is inference running and what models are you evaluating?
[00:40] Sam Torres: yeah — we run a mix; majority is on-prem k8s with custom autoscaler, some endpoints in gcp (vertex) for burst, current models are a 7B open decoder and a 13B we finetuned for summarization. latency at p50 is fine but p99 spikes to 600-800ms on busy sessions.
[00:57] Lena Ortiz: also, we have strict egress caps and need VPC peering; keys are in our KMS, so any private option needs to integrate with that.
[01:08] Priya Patel: thanks — exactly the sort of constraints Optimize is designed for. quick framing: batching reduces per-token compute by aggregating tokens across concurrent requests, but it can add latency if you wait too long to form batches. KV/prefix cache reduces repeated prefix decode costs for chat-like flows. both together usually give the biggest wins for cost without sacrificing p99 if tuned.
[01:34] Priya Patel: (demo) here's a simple cost model: baseline hosted per-token cost X, with batching at our recommended batch sizes you get ~25-40% reduction in per-token GPU time; add KV cache with a 60-80% hit rate on warm sessions and you can drop effective token compute by another 30-50% depending on prefix length.
[01:50] Sam Torres: that 60-80% hit rate — is that realistic? our chats often have variable prefixes.
[01:55] Priya Patel: yep, it depends. prefix cache works best when there are stable system prompts or repeated onboarding prompts. KV cache is per-conversation key-value cache for transformer KV states — if your sessions have repeated turns or many shared system messages, hit rates look like that. we also do automatic prefix clustering to group similar prefixes.
[02:12] Alex Chen: wanted to call out the conservative vs aggressive cache settings: conservative keeps smaller cache, higher miss but safer memory; aggressive caches more prefixes and saves more compute but uses more RAM and can raise memory pressure on the node.
[02:26] Lena Ortiz: memory pressure is our main infra worry — we can't oversubscribe GPUs given other critical workloads.
[02:31] Priya Patel: for that we suggest a hybrid: dedicate a small pool of GPUs for cache-heavy routes — Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools — or use hosted for heavy chat routes and private for sensitive flows. the runtime will route based on policy (latency-first vs cost-first).
[02:50] Mark Delaney: does fallback between hosted and dedicated add latency spikes? we need graceful degradation.
[02:55] Priya Patel: fallback is designed to hit compatible model variants. if a cached variant isn't available we fall back to a cold start route; the routing layer prioritizes low-latency options first and gradually spills to cost-tiered variants. we can set strict SLO-based routing to avoid >200ms p99 violations — that might increase cost a bit.
[03:18] Sam Torres: can you show a concrete example — numbers help.
[03:21] Priya Patel: sure. imagine a 13B model, baseline token compute 1.0 unit. with batching at B=16 average, you reduce to 0.7 units per token. with KV cache hit 70% and average cached prefix length of 25 tokens, effective per-token compute becomes roughly 0.7 * (0.3 + 0.7 * 0.1) — so large savings. (note: approximate math, we'll send detailed worksheet).
[03:46] Alex Chen: note the math is approximate and depends on sequence length distribution; that's why we ask for sample traffic to run a bench.
[03:52] Lena Ortiz: what about cold-starts for short bursts — our traffic is spiky at payroll times. do you have warm pools?
[03:58] Priya Patel: yes, we recommend small warm pools and pre-warming for scheduled events. dedicated capacity supports reserved instances and burst capacity for spikes. also keep small evictable caches for really short bursts.
[04:12] Sam Torres: security — you mentioned KMS support. we must have customer-managed keys and audit logs.
[04:18] Alex Chen: absolutely — Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS/HSM and streams audit logs. priya, quick note on logs?
[04:25] Priya Patel: audit trails and token-level traces are supported; for private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed inside the VPC. network diagrams and SOC2 docs we'll share after this call.
[04:35] Mark Delaney: any work needed from our infra for the pilot?
[04:38] Priya Kumar (Mariner PM): we'd prefer Redwood run the benchmark against our staging via VPC peering; we'll provide test tokens and SLOs.
[04:46] Priya Patel: perfect — we'll coordinate a benchmark that simulates production-turns, include warm/cold mixes, and report p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
[04:57] Alex Chen: i'm going to recap next steps at the end, but quick FYI on pricing structure: hosted pay-as-you-go vs dedicated reserved (monthly commit) — dedicated reduces unit cost but needs a commit; our Optimize tool shows the break-even point given your qps and session characteristics.
[05:15] Sam Torres: what's typical break-even for a company our size?
[05:18] Alex Chen: for steady 24/7 qps above ~600 concurrent tokens/sec for many models, dedicated usually wins; for spiky workloads with low sustained average, hosted + caching can be cheaper. again, we'll model this for your traffic.
[05:31] Sam Torres: any red flags on compliance? we need SOC2 and support for HIPAA-ish data controls — not necessarily HIPAA cert but controls.
[05:39] Priya Patel: we have SOC2 and can provide a compliance pack; for HIPAA-level controls we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and audit log retention.
[05:47] Mark Delaney: do you support query-level redaction or ephemeral tokenization?
[05:51] Priya Patel: yes, Redwood supports pre-send redaction hooks and tokenization; we also support in-flight masking for PII before caching to avoid storing sensitive prefixes.
[05:59] Alex Chen: ok we're at the half-hour mark; do you want us to deep-dive on any particular section or keep this high level and then run the pilot?
[06:06] Sam Torres: let's focus on the concrete pilot steps and scheduling, that'll be most helpful.
[06:10] Priya Patel: great — pilot plan: 1) Mariner provides sample traffic + SLOs; 2) Redwood runs benchmark with three configs (hosted baseline, hosted+optimize, dedicated+optimize); 3) share results with cost per 1M tokens and latency distribution; 4) tune cache settings and rerun.
[06:30] Sam Torres: timeline? we want results within 2 weeks.
[06:33] Alex Chen: we can do an initial run in 5 business days after we get samples, final tuned run in 10. that's consistent with 2-week target.
[06:40] Lena Ortiz: final question on dev effort — how invasive is SDK integration?
[06:44] Priya Patel: SDKs are simple REST/HTTP calls; we also have a tiny client lib for streaming. prefix/KV cache is a runtime feature — no code changes needed other than tagging routes and enabling cache keys for sessions.
[06:57] Mark Delaney: great. any blockers on our side? Sam?
[07:00] Sam Torres: we'll get the sample traffic and SLO doc by end of tomorrow, assign lena as infra contact.
[07:06] Alex Chen: perfect. recap of next steps — Alex to send pilot pricing & commit options, priya to send security docs & demo worksheet, mariner to share sample traffic. we'll schedule the benchmark slot after docs exchanged. any other questions?
[07:23] Priya Kumar: none here. thanks all.
[07:25] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and i put the action items in crm. bye.
[07:30] [end]
